nodes.name: Tasks is available in early access. It is not generally…
nodes.text: Tasks is available in early access. It is not generally available and not sold as a standalone product. This essay describes how it works and why, so you can see where it fits; details may still change, and What’s new? will say when they do.

nodes.name: Tasks is deliberately basic: shared tasks that people,…
nodes.text: Tasks is deliberately basic: shared tasks that people, external agents and Null work on with the same operations and the same permissions. Each task belongs to one location—the workspace, a product or a project—and anyone who can see that location can read and edit its tasks. There are no separate Tasks roles to manage.

nodes.name: Work is followed in list, board and timeline views, with…
nodes.text: Work is followed in list, board and timeline views, with sub-tasks for larger pieces of work, dependencies between tasks, comments with @mentions, and in-app notifications.

nodes.name: Every task has a **mode** and a separate **status**. The…
nodes.text: Every task has a **mode** and a separate **status**. The mode says what kind of work is wanted: Plan means work out what to do and write it down; Build means do the work. The status—backlog, to do, in progress, in review, done or canceled—says where the work stands.

nodes.name: Keeping them apart avoids a common confusion. A task can…
nodes.text: Keeping them apart avoids a common confusion. A task can be in progress while still being planned. “Ready to build” is one explicit step that switches a planned task to Build, and anyone who can edit the task may take it. Agents are guided to switch to Build only when a person explicitly asks, and the activity log records who did it and through which agent.

nodes.name: How an agent picks up work.
nodes.text: ## How an agent picks up work.

nodes.name: A person assigns a task to their agent in the app. The…
nodes.text: A person assigns a task to their agent in the app. The server never pushes work into a local agent; the harness asks for it. That can be a direct request (“work on T-123”), a request for the next ready task, or a scheduled check in the harness.

nodes.name: In Plan mode, the agent reads the task, its comments, the…
nodes.text: In Plan mode, the agent reads the task, its comments, the repository and the relevant Memory files, writes the plan into the task, moves it to review and stops. In Build mode, it claims the task so the team can see who is working on it, reports progress at milestones and moves the task to review with a summary of what changed and how it was verified. It does not mark work done unless asked.

nodes.name: An agent connection needs its own Tasks capability—none,…
nodes.text: An agent connection needs its own Tasks capability—none, read or edit—which is off by default and independent of Memory, Grid, Locale and Secrets. Agents act for their member, and the agent name shown on a change is a label that never grants anything.

nodes.name: Every write carries a request ID, so a retried call…
nodes.text: Every write carries a request ID, so a retried call returns the saved result instead of writing twice. Description changes name the revision they were based on, so an agent never overwrites a person’s edits. Attachments live in their own private storage, and a link to a Memory file never grants access to it. The agent tools ship in the NullDull client.
